blocks.explanation:
Yeh infinite (kabhi khatam na hone wali) A.G.P. hai jis mein \(|r| < 1\) hai, is liye terms chhote hote jate hain aur kul jama ek fixed number ban jata hai. Tareeqa wahi multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract hai, bas ab koi aakhri term nahi jo minus ho, aur beech mein infinite G.P. banti hai jis ka sum \(\frac{\text{pehla term}}{1 - r}\) hota hai.
Upar \(1, 3, 5, 7, \ldots\) A.P. hai, neeche 2 ki powers, yani G.P. ratio \(r = \frac12\).
Plan: \(S\) aur \(\frac12 S\) shift kar ke likho, minus karo, infinite G.P. ka sum lagao, aur aakhir mein 6.8.2 wale \(S_\infty\) formula se tasdeeq karo.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(1 + \frac{3}{2} + \frac{5}{4} + \frac{7}{8} + \cdots\); \(a = 1, d = 2, b = 1, r = \frac{1}{2}\)
Humein find karna hai: infinity tak ka sum \(S\).
Tareeqa: \(|r| = \frac12 < 1\), is liye sum mojood hai (terms zero ki taraf jate hain). Phir \(r\) se multiply, shift aur minus.

\(S\) aur \(\frac12 S\) likhein
\[S = 1 + \dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{5}{4} + \dfrac{7}{8} + \cdots\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2}S = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{5}{8} + \cdots\]
Kyun: \(\frac12\) se multiply karne par har denominator double ho gaya. Ek jagah shift kar ke likha taake \(\frac{3}{2}\) ke neeche \(\frac{1}{2}\), \(\frac{5}{4}\) ke neeche \(\frac{3}{4}\) aaye, yani same denominator.

Minus karein
\[\tfrac{1}{2}S = 1 + \dfrac{2}{2} + \dfrac{2}{4} + \dfrac{2}{8} + \cdots\]
\[= 1 + \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \cdots\right)\]
Kyun: Left side \(S - \frac12 S = \frac12 S\). Right side par har jore ka farq upar 2 deta hai, jaise \(\frac{3}{2} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{2}\), \(\frac{5}{4} - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{2}{4}\). Pehla term 1 akela rehta hai. Infinite series mein koi aakhri term nahi hota jo minus ho; \(|r| < 1\) ki wajah se door ke terms waise bhi zero ke qareeb ho jate hain.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{2}{2}, \frac{2}{4}, \ldots\) ko \(1, \frac12, \ldots\) likh lena behtar hai, G.P. saaf nazar aati hai.

Infinite G.P. ka sum
\[1 + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \cdots = \dfrac{1}{1 - \frac{1}{2}} = 2\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2}S = 1 + 2 = 3\]
\[S = 6\]
Kyun: Infinite G.P. ka sum \(\frac{\text{pehla term}}{1 - r}\) hai: \(\frac{1}{1/2} = 2\). Phir \(\frac12 S = 3\), dono taraf 2 se multiply kar ke \(S = 6\).

Formula se tasdeeq
\[S_\infty = \dfrac{ab}{1 - r} + \dfrac{dbr}{(1 - r)^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\frac{1}{2}} + \dfrac{2 \cdot \frac{1}{2}}{\frac{1}{4}}\]
\[= 2 + 4 = 6 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: 6.8.2 ka formula \(a = 1, d = 2, b = 1, r = \frac12\) ke saath bhi 6 deta hai. Partial sums bhi dekhein: \(1, 2.5, 3.75, 4.625, \ldots\) dheere dheere 6 ki taraf barh rahe hain.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh infinite (kabhi khatam na hone wali) A.G.P. hai jis mein \(|r| < 1\) hai, is liye terms chhote hote jate hain aur kul jama ek fixed number ban jata hai. Tareeqa wahi multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract hai, bas ab koi aakhri term nahi jo minus ho, aur beech mein infinite G.P. banti hai jis ka sum \(\frac{\text{pehla term}}{1 - r}\) hota hai.
Upar \(2, 5, 8, 11, \ldots\) A.P. hai (\(d = 3\)), neeche 3 ki powers, yani G.P. ratio \(\frac13\).
Plan: \(S\) aur \(\frac13 S\) shift kar ke likho, minus karo, infinite G.P. ka sum lagao, phir formula se tasdeeq.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(2 + \frac{5}{3} + \frac{8}{9} + \cdots\); \(a = 2, d = 3, b = 1, r = \frac{1}{3}\)
Humein find karna hai: infinity tak ka sum \(S\).
Tareeqa: \(|r| = \frac13 < 1\), is liye sum mojood hai. \(r\) se multiply, shift aur minus.

\(S\) aur \(\frac13 S\) likhein
\[S = 2 + \dfrac{5}{3} + \dfrac{8}{9} + \dfrac{11}{27} + \cdots\]
\[\tfrac{1}{3}S = \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{5}{9} + \dfrac{8}{27} + \cdots\]
Kyun: \(\frac13\) se multiply karne par har denominator 3 guna ho gaya. Shift kar ke likha taake 3 ke neeche 3, 9 ke neeche 9 aaye.

Minus karein
\[\tfrac{2}{3}S = 2 + \dfrac{3}{3} + \dfrac{3}{9} + \dfrac{3}{27} + \cdots\]
\[= 2 + \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{9} + \cdots\right)\]
Kyun: Left side \(S - \frac13 S = \frac23 S\). Right side par har jore se upar \(d = 3\) bachta hai: \(\frac{5 - 2}{3} = \frac33\), \(\frac{8 - 5}{9} = \frac39\). Pehla term 2 akela rehta hai. Phir \(\frac{3}{3} = 1\), \(\frac{3}{9} = \frac13\) likh kar G.P. saaf ho gayi.

Infinite G.P. ka sum
\[1 + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{9} + \cdots = \dfrac{1}{1 - \frac{1}{3}} = \dfrac{3}{2}\]
\[\tfrac{2}{3}S = 2 + \tfrac{3}{2} = \tfrac{7}{2}\]
\[S = \tfrac{7}{2} \cdot \tfrac{3}{2} = \tfrac{21}{4}\]
Kyun: Infinite G.P. ka sum \(\frac{1}{2/3} = \frac32\). Phir \(\frac23 S = \frac72\), aur \(S\) akela karne ke liye dono taraf \(\frac32\) se multiply kiya.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac23 S = \frac72\) se \(S = \frac72 \cdot \frac23\) likhna ghalat hai; ulta fraction \(\frac32\) lagta hai.

Formula se tasdeeq
\[S_\infty = \dfrac{ab}{1 - r} + \dfrac{dbr}{(1 - r)^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{2}{\frac{2}{3}} + \dfrac{3 \cdot \frac{1}{3}}{\frac{4}{9}}\]
\[= 3 + \dfrac{9}{4} = \dfrac{21}{4} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Formula mein \(a = 2, d = 3, b = 1, r = \frac13\) rakhne se bhi \(\frac{21}{4} = 5.25\) aata hai. Pehle chaar terms ka jama \(2 + 1.67 + 0.89 + 0.41 \approx 4.96\) hai, jo 5.25 ke qareeb pohanch raha hai.
